The compact convex set \(V\le8\varepsilon^2\) is absorbing and invariant. The difference energy obeys \(\dot W\le-W/4\) there because \(0\le r\le3/20\), giving a unique globally exponentially attracting \(2\pi\)-periodic Duffing response by Brouwer and contraction. Anti-periodicity and \(\alpha\ne0\) give \(\operatorname{sgn}J=\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha\beta)\) for \(\beta\ne0\), with \(J=0\) exactly for \(\beta=0\). Integrable transients yield \(z=Jt+P+L+O(e^{-t/8})\). The analytic resonant expansion \(X=\varepsilon\sin t+B\varepsilon^3U+O(\varepsilon^5)\) has \(\langle\sin t\,U\rangle=0\) and \(\langle\sin^4t\rangle=3/8\), so \(J=\alpha\beta\varepsilon^2/2+\alpha\beta^3\varepsilon^4/16+O(\varepsilon^6)\). Symbolic identities and 36 finite numerical tilt checks passed; the analytical proof alone establishes the infinite parameter and initial-state quantifiers.

value.rationale: The source introduces a three-dimensional exponential enhancement to a forced Duffing oscillator as a numerical chaotic-signal model. This theorem rigorously separates a stable synchronizing base from an axially unbounded complete flow for every initial condition on an explicit continuum of parameters, with a sharp zero-tilt transport reversal, and a non-obvious resonant quartic coefficient independent of the strength of the cubic force. These results restrict the interpretation of bounded attractors for this exact model and quantify transport, rather than simply recompute fixed points or restate elementary monotonicity. No global result is claimed in the large-drive chaotic regimes.
